 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 23-09-2023 at about 11.20 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a two-wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-02-HK-4532, near Malleshwaram 19th Route,
old BJP office, near Malleshwaram.

At the same time, a KTM bike bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KP-3917, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed, endangering to human life and property, came and dashed against the two-wheeler of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was student and was hale and healthy.
Due to accidental injuries, she is unable to go to school, unable to attend the classes for a period of 6 months, she has lost her school days and education, she has lost her carrier and golden life.
The Malleshwaram Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the KTM bike bearing No.KA-04-KP-3917 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KP-3917 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the vehicle has been falsely implicated for unlawful gains by the petitioner.
The alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.

Hence, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 and is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Further it is contended that, the compensation if any has to be claimed from the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-HK-4532 in which the petitioner was riding pillion.
The owner and insurer of the said motorcycle are necessary parties to the present claim petition.
Hence, the petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-3917 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-3917 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532 and self fall from the said motorcycle.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Deputy Manager of the respondent No.2 insurance company, there is absolutely no corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by respondent No.2 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532 and self fall from the said motorcycle.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KP-3917 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her right hand and other parts of the body in the said accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length

,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to his negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
13. But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the P.W.1/ rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532 was riding the same along with three pillion riders.

There are every chances that, due to four person travelling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two person,
there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532 is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.

But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of four persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim and all the three pillion riders being minor children, this Court is of the further opinion that, holding the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02- HK-4532 liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.

14. The Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the accident has taken place on the left side of 30 feet wide Malleshwaram 19 route road, near old BJP Office, Malleshwaram,
Bengaluru, in between offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-3917 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.9,
the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there is no negligence on the part the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident Dawlath Sarah N vs Ashish Bangalore Lokanath on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84123394/
5 had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-3917.

sentences.text: Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.11 final report/charge-sheet, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917.

Admittedly, the said charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KP-3917.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.13 wound certificate, Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.22 case-sheet, Ex.P.23 clinical notes and Ex.P.24 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered displaced fracture shaft of right humerus.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 23-09-2023 at about 11.20 a.m., on Malleshwaram 19 route, near old BJP Office, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917.
But, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.

For the reasons stated supra, this Court has held that, there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of petitioner's motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK- 4532 also in the cause of accident, to the extent of 10%.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917 and she has sustained grievous injuries.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained displaced fracture shaft of right humerus and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.17.
As per Ex.P.17, the date of birth of the petitioner is 21-04-2013.
The accident has taken place on 23-09-2023 at about 11.20 A.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 10 years.
In the case in hand, petitioner is admittedly a minor of the age of 10 years as on the date of accident and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
20.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396, has clearly held that, "Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts, we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc. should be, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; up to 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; up to 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.

sentences.text:
For permanent disability up to 10%, it should be Rs.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick."
21.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above cited decision, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
i) Pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts, etc. and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability:
The petitioner has averred that due to accidental injuries, he has sustained grievous injuries and he has suffered disability.
Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability,

has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered displaced fracture shaft of right humerus and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. CRIF with TENS.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 33% to the right arm and 11% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.13 wound certificate,
Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.22 case sheet, Ex.P.23 clinical Dawlath Sarah N vs Ashish Bangalore Lokanath on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84123394/
7 notes and Ex.P.24 x-ray are clear evident that, the petitioner has suffered the above mentioned injury and she has undergone surgery for the said injury.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 23-09-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 12-04- 2025, which is after lapse of one year and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, right humerus fracture is united and implants have been removed.
Further he has clearly admitted that, as the petitioner is of the tender age, after passage of time the disability will be reduced.

Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

As per the ratio laid down in the above decision, since the disability to the whole body of the petitioner is 8%, he is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
under this head.
ii) Discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.,
fracture shaft of right humerus and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. CRIF with TENS.

As per Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summaries (total 2),
the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days in Manipal Hospital,
Bengaluru and Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru.

During the period of hospitalization of the petitioner, her parents would have definitely undergone some discomfort,
inconvenience and loss of earnings.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that,

awarding compensation of Rs.32,000/-
under this particular head would be just and reasonable.
iii) Medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, food &
nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 2 medical bills, as per Ex.P.16.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.2,14,859/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,14,859/- under the head of medical expenses.
iv) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summaries (total 2), the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru and Apollo Hospital,
Bengaluru.

Her parents might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment Dawlath Sarah N vs Ashish Bangalore Lokanath on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84123394/
8 during that period.

v) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Bhashyam Nagar, Bengaluru North,
Bengaluru, the accident has taken place on Malleshwaram 19 route, near old BJP Office,
Malleshwaram, Bengaluru and she has taken treatment at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru and Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places

,
compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vi) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the fracture is united and implants are removed.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner is in need of any further treatment for the injuries suffered in the accident.
In such circumstances, question of awarding compensation to the petitioner towards future medical expenses does not arise.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head future medical expenses.

22. Hence, the petitioner is entitled to the compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Pain and suffering already 1,00,000-00 undergone and to be suffered in future,
mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts, etc. and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability 2. Discomfort, inconvenience and 32,000-00 loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization 3.
Medical and incidental 2,14,859-00 expenses during the period of hospitalisation for 4 days 4. Food and nourishment 3,200-00 expenses 5.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 6.
Future medical expenses Nil Total 3,55,059-00 90% of Total Rs.3,19,553-00

In all,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,19,553/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- KP-3917.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.8, the rider of offending vehicle by name Ashish B.L. S/o B.C. Lokanath was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA-0520060006622 to ride offending motorcycle and it was valid from 06-09-2016 to 27-06-2026 and the offending vehicle was insured by the respondent No.2 insurance company vide policy No.67140131230900002100 and it was valid from 23-08- 2023 to 22-08-2028.

sentences.text: Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,19,553/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,19,553/- (Rupees three lakh nineteen thousand five hundred and fifty three only), with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the above compensation amount, 70% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized/scheduled bank, till she attains the age of majority and the remaining 30% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the natural guardian/father of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 23-09-2023, at about 11.20 a.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the KTM Bike bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KP-3917 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 23-09-2023 at about 11.20 a.m., on Malleshwaram 19 route, near old BJP Office, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Deputy Manager of the respondent No.2 insurance company, there is absolutely no corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by respondent No.2 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532 and self fall from the said motorcycle.
On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KP-3917 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her right hand and other parts of the body in the said accident.
,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to his negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
There are every chances that, due to four person travelling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two person,
there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532 is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.
But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of four persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim and all the three pillion riders being minor children, this Court is of the further opinion that, holding the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02- HK-4532 liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.9,
the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there is no negligence on the part the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HK-4532,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident Dawlath Sarah N vs Ashish Bangalore Lokanath on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84123394/
5 had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-3917.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KP-3917 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

opennyai_summary.decision:
22. Hence, the petitioner is entitled to the compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Pain and suffering already 1,00,000-00 undergone and to be suffered in future,
mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts, etc. and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability 2. Discomfort, inconvenience and 32,000-00 loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization 3.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 6.
In all,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,19,553/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,19,553/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,19,553/- (Rupees three lakh nineteen thousand five hundred and fifty three only), with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the above compensation amount, 70% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized/scheduled bank, till she attains the age of majority and the remaining 30% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the natural guardian/father of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
